span.label: Hannula and Ranganath's fMRI study of short-term associative memory, read for what it shows about the hippocampal contribution to holding novel associations in mind.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: How — at which task phase and by what signal — does the hippocampus support short-term memory for novel associative information?

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the task being performed sets the amplitude of the hippocampal response to novel or familiar input, so top-down task demands determine whether match or mismatch produces the larger signal
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The hippocampus may hold associations through transient changes in synaptic efficacy rather than sustained firing, which would explain why no delay-period signal appears
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Active maintenance might still occur by a mechanism fMRI cannot see, such as theta/gamma oscillations
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The hippocampus is proposed to act as a comparator, detecting discrepancies between predictions from past experience and current input
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The commentary's own resolution of the conflicting match/mismatch results: the size of the hippocampal response to novelty depends on what task is being performed, with top-down influence present in explicit recognition and absent in automatic detection
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Under explicit recognition the pattern resembles match enhancement in monkey inferotemporal and perirhinal cortex, whereas automatic novelty detection may show the comparator signal uncontaminated by top-down input
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The commentary's central conclusion rests on a null delay-period result in the study it reviews, which it flags as requiring caution.
span.note: what this limits: the commentary's central conclusion, which rests on an absence: ALTHOUGH CAUTION IS ADVISED IN INTERPRETING SUCH A NULL FINDING, THIS RESULT DOES SUGGEST THAT PERSISTENT NEURAL FIRING IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS DOES NOT OCCUR DURING THE DELAY PERIOD
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Absent confidence ratings, a performance/confidence confound in the match-versus-mismatch comparison it relies on cannot be entirely excluded.
span.note: what this limits: the match-versus-mismatch comparison it relies on: WITHOUT CONFIDENCE RATING DATA, IT IS DIFFICULT TO ENTIRELY EXCLUDE THE POSSIBILITY THAT SUBJECTS MAY HAVE BEEN MORE CONFIDENT IN MAKING (CORRECT) MATCH ... JUDGMENTS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The commentary's own caution: without confidence ratings, better performance on match trials cannot be fully separated from the neural difference attributed to match
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, and it is a re-raising rather than a new objection: THE AUTHORS CAREFULLY CONSIDERED AND DISCOUNTED SUCH AN EFFECT
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The central conclusion about maintenance rests on an absence of difference, which the commentary flags as a null result
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - the maintenance conclusion is a null finding
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The formal models that would make the comparator account testable do not yet exist in the required form
span.note: what this limits: the comparator account: ONE IMPORTANT DIRECTION FOR FUTURE RESEARCH WILL BE TO DEVELOP AND EMPIRICALLY TEST FORMAL COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF RECOGNITION MEMORY ... AND AUTOMATIC NOVELTY PROCESSING

span.label: contradicts → Kumaran and Maguire (2006)
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER THE MEMORY JUDGMENT IS EXPLICIT OR INCIDENTAL. 'Quotation withheld (i.e., subjects are not required to make explicit recognition memory judgments), A QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT PATTERN OF FINDINGS HAS BEEN OBSERVED with hippocampal activation maximal under conditions of mismatch rather than match.' The direction of the hippocampal effect REVERSES on a task-instruction parameter - the strongest form this field takes, because the two literatures are not in conflict at all once the parameter is named. Q-447.

span.label: perirhinal cortex —contrasted-with→ hippocampus
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHAT KIND OF INFORMATION IS BEING HELD. 'Whereas THE PERIRHINAL CORTEX APPEARS TO SUPPORT SHORT-TERM MEMORY FOR NOVEL OBJECT INFORMATION, neuropsychological evidence suggests that the hippocampus is CRITICAL WHEN ASSOCIATIVE INFORMATION IS INVOLVED.' Both structures support short-term memory; the division is BY CONTENT, NOT BY DURATION - which is the point, since duration is what the literature usually divides them by. Q-468. · strength of the relation: 1

span.label: allocentric —distinct-from→ egocentric
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS THE REFERENCE FRAME, AND THE MANIPULATION THAT ENFORCES IT IS GIVEN. 'Quotation withheld, subjects were asked to FORM A MENTAL IMAGE OF THE SCENE ROTATED 90 [degrees].' The two frames are not observed and distinguished - one is INDUCED BY AN INSTRUCTION, so the result is conditional on subjects complying with it. Kravitz2011[1] in this corpus gives the same axis as an anatomical tendency, hedged on both sides. Q-478. · strength of the relation: 1

The span's main clause is this paper's own finding that persistent firing does NOT occur in the hippocampus during the delay period; the entorhinal operationalisation is carried only by the trailing 'AS IS THOUGHT TO OCCUR IN THE ENTORHINAL CORTEX'. Nothing about the entorhinal cortex was measured here. · strength of the relation: 0.8

span.label: Hippocampal activity measured during the sample (encoding) phase predicted whether the later recognition judgment would be correct.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A subsequent-memory effect in the perirhinal cortex appeared only in the sample phase, consistent with that region encoding item-specific rather than associative information.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Hippocampal activity during the 11 s delay did not differ between later-correct and later-incorrect trials, arguing against persistent hippocampal firing as the maintenance mechanism.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On correct trials, hippocampal activation was higher for match displays than for either type of mismatch display.
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: The authors used a region-of-interest analysis to demonstrate - THE EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW ATTRIBUTES THE WORK TO SOMEBODY ELSE. The cited name is the subject of a result verb and the sentence carries no first-person marker, so the finding, quantity or definition is the CITED author's rather than this record's. The claim is true and the quote is verbatim - what is wrong is whose result the corpus says it is. Nothing edited, nothing withdrawn: the row is marked so a page can name the source. Where the record is a commentary or review, its `claim_relations` layer usually already names the paper being discussed - the record knows at one layer and forgets at another.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The direction of the hippocampal match/mismatch response reverses when novelty is incidental rather than the object of an explicit recognition judgment, with activation then peaking for mismatch.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The hippocampus contributes to short-term memory for novel associations at encoding and retrieval but apparently not during active maintenance.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Finding a hippocampal subsequent-memory effect at test as well as at sample excludes the alternative that sample-phase activity merely reflected encoding of the individual objects rather than the object-location associations.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
